title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has released its response to a 2020 committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its approach to making AI safer and more accountable. It commits to strengthening regulations, setting clear standards, and improving oversight for AI systems used in public services.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee the use of AI in UK exams and qualifications, focusing on fairness, accuracy and transparency. The document sets guidelines to help exam bodies, training providers and students use AI responsibly.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright‑protected materials are used in training and developing AI systems, and evaluates the legal and ethical consequences of that practice. It offers recommendations and policy options for balancing creators’ rights with the advancement of artificial intelligence.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to strengthen AI governance, boost research and innovation, and address ethical and safety concerns. The response signals a commitment to ensuring that AI development in the UK remains responsible, transparent, and aligned with public interest while supporting economic growth.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee reviewing artificial intelligence in relation to public standards, including how AI should be integrated into public policy and regulatory frameworks. It also provides a FAQ section that clarifies key concepts, expectations, and procedures to guide stakeholders in understanding the committee’s work.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee in response to an inquiry about how AI should be governed. The submission aims to influence policy recommendations for responsible AI development and oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how advances in artificial intelligence will influence the rules and standards for medical products, ensuring they remain safe and effective. It calls for adopting the AI White Paper principles to guide regulatory practices, promote transparency, and protect patients.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets a vision for the organisation to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI‑powered defence force for its size. It focuses on building advanced AI capabilities, partnerships and safeguards to achieve this leadership goal.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness AI’s benefits, such as improving safety, efficiency and sustainability. At the same time it outlines safeguards and risk‑management measures to address privacy, safety and ethical concerns that could arise from AI use in transportation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright‑protected works are currently being used to train and improve AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It summarizes recent findings, highlights challenges, and recommends steps to balance AI innovation with respect for copyright holders.
